intro:
Amos, third of The Twelve (Minor Prophets), is a shepherd and fig farmer from Judah sent north to prophesy against Israel's elite. Not a professional prophet—God calls him from tending flocks. His message: religious festivals and sacrifices mean nothing when you're oppressing the poor. 'Let justice roll down like waters, righteousness like a never-failing stream!'

Amos delivers five visions of judgment (locusts, fire, plumb line, summer fruit, altar) and announces: 'The end has come for my people Israel.' He condemns neighboring nations too, but Israel gets the harshest word because they knew better.

Despite doom, ends with hope: 'I will restore David's fallen shelter... plant Israel in their own land, never to be uprooted.'
outro: Amos is the prophet of social justice—God hates worship disconnected from ethics. The wealthy in Samaria are condemned for trampling the poor while having religious services. Amos shows that privilege increases responsibility. His 'plumb line' vision means God measures societies by His standard of justice. Modern application: faith must impact how we treat the marginalized.
